research_scope: Australian NEW BEV Audi and Porsche: exact current manufacturer listings; MY27 announced/orderable arrivals; older and residual stock cohorts; primary-source technical/price/warranty and exact dealer audit. Includes Porsche Cayenne BEVs. Research only.

catalogue_decision.reason: 32 current manufacturer-listed model rows are not 32 verified available NEW units. Eight Audi future rows and seven older exact rows are distinct cohorts. Porsche 27 explicit battery branches are scoped inside 25 models. No qualifying fresh exact NEW advertisement accepted in bounded stock audit; this is not evidence of nationwide absence. Current price/certification/technical gaps remain held.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

technical_disclaimers.content: PS (PferdeStärke, German for horsepower) is the standard unit used in the European Union to measure the power output of a motor in ‘metric horsepower’.

The published kilometre (km) range figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real world consumption and km range you will experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

The published charging times and power capabilities are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG. The actual achievable real world charging times and power you will experience can be less than the published data depending on a number of factors such as the ambient conditions, battery size, battery state of health/age, the amount of charge the battery has, and the type of charger, and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. We recommend charging to 80 per cent to assist in maximising your vehicle’s battery range and battery life over time.

The published consumption (l/100km and Wh/km), and emissions (g/km) figures for vehicles are based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG (with a fully charged battery for electric and hybrid vehicles), conducted in accordance with the applicable Australian Design Rule (ADR) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. Specifically, the published kilometre (km) range figure for battery electric vehicles is the WLTP combined vehicle high range based on laboratory test results from Porsche AG conducted in accordance with the applicable ADR using the Worldwide harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) and is for vehicle comparison purposes only. The actual achievable real-world consumption you experience can be less than the published data, depending on numerous factors such as speed, traffic and weather conditions, driving habits, elevation change, how much weight the vehicle is carrying, battery state of health/age, use of vehicle features/accessories such as heating or air-conditioning, and wheels/tyres among others.

motor_count.locator: SQ6 e-tron > SQ6 e-tron models bring

field_provenance.exact_text: The SQ6 e-tron models bring even greater performance to the ranks, with an electric motor mounted to both the front and rear axles producing a whopping 360kW of power which grows to 380kW with the launch control in play. That means torque of 275Nm up front and 580Nm on the rear, for 4.3 second 0 to 100km/h time. Obviously the SQ6 e-tron employs a larger 100kWh battery (94.9kWh net), but thanks to its 270 kW DC fast charging capabilities, it takes no longer than the Q6 e-tron to charge from 10 to 80 percent.

field_provenance.exact_text: Audi Australia has announced new equipment and pricing for the 2027 Q6 e-tron and SQ6 e-tron models, as well as a limited time offer on Q6 e-tron sport edition models available now. Building on the tremendous appeal of the Q6 e-tron models, the increased levels of standard appointment coupled with sharp pricing is designed to allow customers to take advantage of eligible Government electric vehicle (EV) incentives on Q6 e-tron and SQ6 e-tron models arriving in the first half of next year.

value.feature: 21-inch Audi Sport wheels and adaptive air suspension

field_provenance.exact_text: The SQ6 e-tron models ride on 21-inch Audi Sport alloy wheels which show off the standard red brake callipers, with adaptive air suspension providing a ‘magic carpet-like’ ride.

value.feature: AR head-up display and 705 W / 16-speaker B&O audio

field_provenance.exact_text: Inside the SQ6 e-tron also gets pneumatically adjustable lumbar support with massage function for the front seats and Dinamica material is used extensively throughout the interior. Colour ambient lighting with 30 selectable colours and dynamic light interaction is part of the standard interior offering along with a three-spoke sport leather steering wheel with flat top and bottom, multifunction paddles and electrically adjusted steering column. The augmented head-up display shows speed, navigation and assistance information and there are dual charging capacity USB interfaces in the front as well as two high charging capacity USB interfaces in the rear. There is also a 705-watt Bang & Olufsen 3D premium sound system which features 16 speakers including subwoofer and centre speaker, as well as a 16-channel amplifier.

Building on the tremendous appeal of the Q6 e-tron models, the increased levels of standard appointment coupled with sharp pricing is designed to allow customers to take advantage of eligible Government electric vehicle (EV) incentives on Q6 e-tron and SQ6 e-tron models arriving in the first half of next year.

field_provenance.exact_text: Inside the SQ6 e-tron also gets pneumatically adjustable lumbar support with massage function for the front seats and Dinamica material is used extensively throughout the interior. Colour ambient lighting with 30 selectable colours and dynamic light interaction is part of the standard interior offering along with a three-spoke sport leather steering wheel with flat top and bottom, multifunction paddles and electrically adjusted steering column. The augmented head-up display shows speed, navigation and assistance information and there are dual charging capacity USB interfaces in the front as well as two high charging capacity USB interfaces in the rear. There is also a 705-watt Bang & Olufsen 3D premium sound system which features 16 speakers including subwoofer and centre speaker, as well as a 16-channel amplifier.

comparison_rules: Never combine ADR81/02 with WLTP or convert cycles.
No station rating equals vehicle DC peak. Charging windows and ideal conditions stay attached.
Separate normal power/acceleration from launch-control figures.
Gross and net battery capacities separately sourced.
Wheel standard equipment does not certify range test wheels.
Cargo seats/measurement/loading method remain explicit and null when absent.
Manufacturer listing or order invitation does not prove completed order acceptance; NEW ad does not prove physical stock.
MY25/MY26/MY27 and exact production date never silently merged.
Optional packs/wheels remain features/options; no Cartesian SKU creation.
Use explicit MY2027 model codes; do not transplant MY2025/MY2026 or ADR/ECE figures.
WLTP Vehicle High is retained exactly, never asserted as single certified all-option or wheel-specific range.
Power up to, overboost/launch-control power, and option-coded performance are distinct.
Gross and net energy stay distinct; net is null when exact evidence is absent.
Battery branches are established only by exact model technical rows/configurator option evidence; no grade/pack/wheel Cartesian products.
A charging station rating and an AC time test do not prove fitted vehicle charging hardware.
Cargo V-codes, loading height and seat position remain attached. Do not compare unqualified litres across them.
Cayenne 3000/3500 kg braked towing depends on extending/fixed towbar; never flatten this option dependency.
Configurator existence is not accepted order; advertised unit is not physical-stock verification.
Price for equipment and unselected-dealer totals are not vehicle MLP or driveaway.
Dated launch prices remain history only; current price null unless exact current amount and basis verified.
scope_limitations: No dealer contact, customer order or purchase attempted.
Current Audi configurator and price layer server snapshots expose shells/nullable prices; no claimed live final vehicle quote.
A6/S6 primary historical plans are not current availability.
PHEV/ICE Q8, A6 and Q6 namesakes excluded.
No national physical-stock census, dealer contact, accepted-order check or delivery commitment.
Default configurator price returned equipment-only subtotal; live dealer-specific vehicle quote not obtained.
Primary public APIs are reached via the current website technical-data component; model year is corroborated by current exact code card and configurator.
Standard equipment feeds can include baseline and upgrade overlaps; current default configurator used where checked. Raw source claims remain inspectable.
Macan/Cayenne usable battery energy is held if not explicitly stated in exact current AU model source.
No price/range/spec from petrol, diesel or PHEV namesakes admitted.
No exhaustive national inventory crawl; no dealer contacts, stock reservation or factory-order acceptance confirmation.
Two raw HTTP fetches (Brisbane inventory and Sydney South Macan campaign) returned Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden; not retried using an alternate access route.
Observed tool session later reported network approval cancelled; completed snapshots and manifest survived and were validated locally.
Cayenne BEV subtype stock and Australian Sport Turismo market presence remain unverified; generic global variant filters are insufficient.
